summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (88/295)

data.turoyo: Gəmmaṣənno raġlax w mhaláx w mwaḏ̣áy w tax!
data.translation: Ich werde deinen Fuß anbinden, und dann geh und wasch dich und komm!

rationale: First Imperativ box, overt female addressee.

data.translation: Aber ich werde gehen und wenigstens erst die Waschung vollziehen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: clear 1sg.f ablution form.

data.turoyo: Gdəzzino mwaḏ̣yono w gdoṯina, w xəd aṯto w gawro.
data.translation: Ich will gehen und die Waschung vollziehen, und dann sind wir wie Mann und Frau.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: ablution before the proposed meeting.

data.turoyo: i naqqa d kəmwaḏe u malla, maṭina l qəm u gəmrək.
data.translation: when the mullah was performing his ablutions, we reached the customs post.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell after two round-1 additions and one unresolved inherited comparison; clear finite k-form with an overt masculine subject.

summary: The finite -no forms provide contextual Infectum evidence where the inherited box is marked Infectum (???). The inherited mwaḏ̣e mətwaḏ̣e ??????? remains an unresolved comparison of forms, not a secure second Detransitive analysis.
The female speaker uses -yono and is addressed by Imperativ mwaḏ̣áy. The new material supports the active II ablution verb; self-directed washing does not automatically create a Detransitive section.
The inherited Arabic source and nḏ̣y cross-reference are retained. PrS 16/23 does not establish a second lexical call-to-prayer sense merely because the German describes a minaret and prayer call.

kəmwaḏe adds finite masculine k-Infectum evidence to the two round-1 feminine forms. The old Infectum (???) heading and untranslated mwaḏ̣e mətwaḏ̣e comparison remain inherited unresolved text; this round does not claim the box is new.

The source uses plain ḏ, retained exactly. Self-directed ritual washing does not alone license Detransitive, and the single lexical verb is not a light-verb combination merely because the reader attached that research tag.
Check PrS 16/23 against its edition: does local mwaḏ̣eno ever mean call to prayer, or has the German freely replaced ablution? The supplied Turoyo contains no explicit minaret.
Verify the inherited PrS 36/9 forms mwaḏ̣e and mətwaḏ̣e and whether the latter belongs to a Detransitive paradigm; the supplied occurrences do not settle it.
Does kəmwaḏe here specifically denote ablution, broader prayer preparation or a prayer call? The morning/mullah scene and machine English do not independently settle the old round-1 ambiguity.
Obtain a checked translation; no minaret, audible call or external washing agent is expressed in this verse.
An overt mullah subject and early-morning temporal setting support ritual washing under the inherited meaning; the Jan verse does not itself establish a separate call-to-prayer sense.
